summary: Make metal parts readable using finish zones and a reflected environment instead of a flat gray color.
objective: Rotate the object under the fixed rig: reflections reveal the hub and rim rather than flattening them into one gray disc.
example_prompts: Make metal parts readable using finish zones and a reflected environment instead of a flat gray color.

principles: Separate bare metal, paint and corrosion patches according to the intended construction.
A polished hub and rough rim can express handling and machining; these are art choices until measured.
implementation: Start bare metal regions at metalness 1 and place broad bright and dark reflection features around the object.
Hold geometry and exposure constant while selecting finish. Avoid adding emission to compensate for an unreadable reflection.
Keep wear at plausible contact or handled edges and inspect its scale at the intended camera distance.
observable_checks: Rotate the object under the fixed rig: reflections reveal the hub and rim rather than flattening them into one gray disc.
Painted and bare regions remain distinguishable without depending solely on hue.

known_limits: This is appearance guidance, not electrical conductivity or a measured alloy model.
Authored reusable guidance; no runtime artifact or improvement has been observed for this record.
creative_affordances: Adapt proportions, finish and presentation to the scene; explain deliberate departures from this guidance.

claims.statement: MeshStandardMaterial uses metalness 1 for metallic surfaces and recommends an environment map.
